concept.heading: One span per tool call, one JSON line per log, one id that joins them
paragraphs: When a staff member says 'it sent the wrong receipt', you need the full story of that one request: which tools ran, in what order, with what arguments, how long each took, and what came back. A trace is that story; each hop is a span with a name, attributes, a duration and an outcome. OpenTelemetry is the standard way to produce them, and a span around every tool call is the minimum instrumentation this track ships with.

Logs are the lines inside the hops. As JSON, one object per line, they are searchable and carry a correlation id (one per request) plus the current trace and span ids, so a log line and a span can be joined later in any tool. Plain text logs cannot be joined by anything.

Two rules carry over from Module 3: the arguments attribute is redacted with the same secret list the log filter uses, and nothing in telemetry ever changes behavior. The exporter is injectable: the check captures spans in memory, you print them to the console, and a client can point them at a free self-hosted collector (Langfuse or Phoenix) without touching a tool.
concept.lowCodeEquivalent: The run history of a flow with every action's inputs, outputs and duration. You read those by clicking; here you emit the same record as data a client can keep, search, and show an auditor.

pythonBlock.title: Python you need: contextvars, the OpenTelemetry tracer, context managers again
pythonBlock.intro: A ContextVar is a value scoped to the current request even across threads and async tasks. The tracer's start_as_current_span is a context manager; your trace_tool_call wraps it.
pythonBlock.code:
import contextvars, time, json
from opentelemetry import trace

correlation_id = contextvars.ContextVar("correlation_id", default=None)

@contextmanager
def trace_tool_call(name, arguments):
    tracer = trace.get_tracer("middleware")
    outcome = Outcome()
    started = time.perf_counter()
    with tracer.start_as_current_span(f"tool.{name}") as span:
        span.set_attribute("tool.name", name)
        span.set_attribute("tool.arguments", redact(json.dumps(arguments, default=str)))
        if correlation_id.get():
            span.set_attribute("correlation_id", correlation_id.get())
        try:
            yield outcome
        except Exception as e:
            span.set_attribute("tool.outcome", f"exception:{e.__class__.__name__}")
            raise
        else:
            code = (outcome.result or {}).get("error", {}).get("code") if isinstance(outcome.result, dict) else None
            span.set_attribute("tool.outcome", f"error:{code}" if code else "ok")
        finally:
            span.set_attribute("tool.duration_ms", (time.perf_counter() - started) * 1000)
